title: Throw an empty can into a pedal bin, the lid opened with the pedal only
instruction: Throw the empty can into the pedal bin, opening the lid with the pedal only.
context: Small pedal bins stand in most bathrooms and kitchens, and a can goes into one many times a week. The point of the pedal is that no hand touches the lid: the pedal lifts it through a rod at the back, and it opens only while the pedal is held down. Here the bin stands on a raised step at the robot's working height (the table stands for it), so one gripper does the foot's job. What goes wrong: the lid lifted by hand; the pedal let go while the other hand is still over the opening, so the lid shuts on it; the can dropped before the lid is fully up, so it hits the lid and bounces off; a hard or slanted press slides or tips the light bin; the pedal let go with a snap instead of eased up.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights from the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +305 and -305 mm. (1) A Brabantia NewIcon 3 L pedal bin, concrete grey, standing loose and upright on the table at x 330 mm, y 0, pedal toward the arms, lid hinge at the back. Published: 264 mm high, 168 mm across, 235 mm deep with pedal and hinge, 411 mm high with the lid open, 0.83 kg, non-slip base, soft-close lid. Estimates (est): rim 248 mm up, clear opening 144 mm across, inner bucket floor 50 mm up; lid 0.12 kg on a hinge 7.5 mm behind the body. Linkage (est): the pedal plate (54 x 70 mm, its top 48 mm up, 0.06 kg with its lever) sticks out 54 mm in front of the body; its lever pivots under the floor and its rear end, behind the bucket, lifts a loose push rod (8 x 7 x 214 mm, 15 g) standing in a slot in the back wall; the rod's top lifts a pin under the lid's hinge, so the lid opens. The pedal stops after 30 mm of travel at the plate's middle, where the lid is open 67 degrees. Let go, the lid's own weight pushes the rod and the pedal back up and the hinge's damping closes it softly (about 1.4 s from fully open). Pedal force at the plate's middle (est): 4.8 N to start it moving, 1.5 N at the stop, well within one YAM arm's push (about 1.7 N m at its shoulder joint for 5 N). (2) An empty 330 ml aluminium drink can, plain red, 66 mm across, 115 mm tall, 14 g (est), standing upright on the table at x 260 mm, y 240 mm (left of the bin). The demo grips it across its side 74 to 106 mm up, the top band of the wall under the necked shoulder, at about 5 N a finger. Friction (est): bin base on table 0.8, can 0.6. Nothing else is on the table. (3) Acceptance checks on the bought bin before the first trial (0-10 N spring scale, protractor, kitchen scale): pressing the middle of the pedal down to its stop takes 10 N or less; fully pressed, the lid opens 60 degrees or more; let go from fully open, the lid shuts on its own; the bin weighs 0.7 to 0.95 kg; an empty can squeezed across that band between two 27 mm wide flat pads with 10 N (twice the grip) shows no dent. A bin or can that fails a check is not used.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the bin, its lid and pedal, the push rod, the can and both grippers. In bin: the can's highest point 10 mm or more below the rim, its centre within 72 mm of the bin's axis (top view) and its lowest point no more than 4 mm below the inner bucket's floor. Shut: the lid within 5 degrees of closed on every step of the last 1 s. Still: over the last 1 s the bin and the can each moved under 5 mm and turned under 5 degrees. Bin kept: the bin within 30 mm of where it started and tilted under 5 degrees. Pushed (latched): the lid moved by anything but the pedal linkage, at any step: a gripper's finger zone (a capsule round the last 38 mm of its fingers, 16 mm in radius closed, 57 mm open, larger than the fingers) within 1 mm of the lid; or the lid rising while more than 5 degrees above the angle the pedal's position and the push rod give it (a hand on the lid or the rod); or the lid more than 5 degrees above the rod's angle and not closing for 3 steps, 0.15 s (held open: a free lid falls over 20 degrees a second); or the can within 1 mm of the lid while the lid rises more than 2 degrees above that angle (the can lifting it). Can hit (latched): at any step the can came within 1 mm of the lid (the simulation's margin for a touch; it is stricter than the real check). Fall (latched): the bin tipped over 30 degrees or slid over 100 mm at any step. Score 0 if fall, or the can is not in the bin, or pushed: opening the lid any way but the pedal earns nothing. Otherwise 1.0 if shut, still, bin kept and the can never hit the lid; else 0.5. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: in bin, look down into the bin with the lid held open after the trial: the can rests inside on the bucket floor, not on the rim, and a straight-edge across the rim clears its top by 10 mm (a 10 mm block on the can's top fits under it); shut, a 5 degree mark at the hinge and 30 fps side video of the last 1 s; still, a 5 mm scale beside the bin and the same video; bin kept, tape marks round its base and a 30 mm rule; pushed, 30 fps side video: no frame shows a gripper on the lid or the can lifting it, and the lid is never more than 5 degrees above what the pedal's position gives except while it closes (a chart of pedal travel against lid angle, measured once with the protractor); can hit, the same video: the can seen or heard touching the lid (a near miss that does not touch is not counted in a real trial); fall, a 30 degree angle gauge and a 100 mm rule. Where the can lies inside the bucket and how many tries it takes are not penalised.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The linkage is contact only: the lever's rear nose lifts a loose rod in a slot, the rod's flat top lifts a pin under the lid hinge; the lid's weight returns it and hinge damping (0.10 N m s/rad, est) is the soft close. No spring, no software rule. The round wall is 16 flat slabs with the inner bucket in it; sizes inside the bin, masses, friction and the pedal force are estimates to measure. The can is rigid (cannot dent): the grip is 5 N on its stiff top band.
reset_notes: Take the can out and stand it upright at x 260 mm, y 240 mm. Stand the bin on its marks at x 330 mm, y 0, pedal toward the arms, lid shut, the inner bucket seated. Nothing is consumed; between trials check that the lid shuts on its own from fully open and that the push rod sits on the lever (the pedal up, the lid flat).
